**Setup:** HP DVD RW AD-7701H (slim USB burner), Linux, disc-probe at 5540 kB/s (CAV, 2296 rpm, about 1 deg jitter).

**What happened:** `geo` always stopped (chi2 too high, "a whole-turn count is probably wrong"). The reason is that the track pitch of this disc is not constant: compared with a constant-pitch spiral, the angle wanders by about 150 deg from the inner edge to the outer edge. No constant-pitch preset (DIS or disc-probe) can fit it, which probably explains why the picture does not appear with the default settings.

**What worked:**
1. `geo --ranges 150000-1950832 --chi2-abort 100`: it still stops, but the rungs it gets give a usable base fit.
2. `tools/geo_probe_points.py` (it ships with disc-probe, in its `tools/` folder: https://github.com/Ashley-QwQ/disc-probe/blob/main/tools/geo_probe_points.py) against that fit, every 10000 LBA from 20000 to 2294000 (229 points, plus a first pass of 56). Points measured twice agree within 0.4 deg rms.
3. A smoothing spline through those points as the angle correction (0.3 deg rms; the degree-12 polynomial from `geo_polyfit.py --phi-degree` only got 0.9 deg rms, 3 deg max), passed to `imagedisc.write_iso(..., correction=...)`.
